item.title: [MLB.com] Dodgers activate Pages, Sasaki before Padres series
item.dc:creator: MLB com

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have activated outfielder Andy Pages and right-handed pitcher Roki Sasaki from the injured list ahead of Tuesday's series opener vs. the Padres and optioned right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Pages, 25, has been out since August 21 after fracturing his left hand against the Pirates. The All-Star has played in 128 games, batting .272 with 21 homers and 80 RBI. He is in his third season with the Dodgers and he has played in 400 games with 61 homers and 212 RBI. He was signed by the Dodgers as an international free agent on March 1, 2018 out of La Habana, Cuba.
Sasaki, 24, has been on the injured list since August 27 with a blister on his right middle finger. In his second full season with the Dodgers, he is 5-5 with a 4.60 ERA, including a 2-0 record with a 3.05 ERA since the All-Star break. He has made 33 Major League appearances in his career, posting a 6-6 mark with a 4.57 ERA and 145 strikeouts in 155.2 innings. He joined the Dodgers as an international free agent on January 22, 2025 from Rikuzentakata, Japan.
Sheehan, 26, pitched 5.1 scoreless innings on Sunday against the Giants. He is 5-8 and a 4.57 ERA with the Dodgers in 2026, racking up 132 strikeouts in 112.1 innings. He is in his third season with the Dodgers, recording a 4.13 ERA with a 15-12 record in 51 games (45 starts). He was drafted by the Dodgers in the sixth round of the 2021 First Year Player Draft out of Boston College.
Alfonzo, 26, has played in 13 games for the Dodgers this season, batting .179 with two doubles and four RBI. He was batting .302 with two homers and 25 RBI with Triple-A Oklahoma City this season. He has appeared in 598 minor league games, batting .283 with 33 homers and 291 RBI. He signed with the Dodgers as a minor league free agent on November 17, 2025.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Playoff Bye Clears the Way for Miguel Rojas’ Citizenship Test
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Miguel Rojas is nearing the end of what’s widely expected to be his final regular season as an MLB player, but he’s got a very good reason not to let up off the gas pedal. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers veteran Miguel Rojas is nearing the end of what’s widely expected to be his final regular season as an MLB player, but he’s got a very good reason not to let up off the gas pedal.
Rojas is a native of Venezuela, but he is applying for his United States citizenship, reports Bill Plunkett of the Orange County Register.
That application requires him to take the citizenship test, and that’s where things can get dicey with baseball’s postseason schedule.
Rojas is set to take that test on Oct. 1, which is the third day of the three-game wild card series.
If the Dodgers were to have to play that round of the playoffs, it “would complicate his travel” to take the exam, Plunkett wrote on social media.
How likely are the Dodgers to get a bye for the wild card round?
Fortunately for Rojas — and the Dodgers as a whole — they seem to have a good hold on the second seed in the National League, which includes a bye for the wild card round.
As of Tuesday morning, the Dodgers have a four game lead over the third-place Atlanta Braves, and with only six regular season games remaining for each team, the Braves are running out of time to make up ground.
As long as the Dodgers can hold off the Braves, Rojas will be available to take his citizenship test, and the injury-plagued Dodgers will also get a few extra days to heal up ahead of a grueling October.
A last dance for Miguel Rojas
Aside from getting his American citizenship, Rojas can also use that time off to soak up his last season as an MLB player.
The hero of the 2025 World Series doesn’t really have anything left to prove, but he told Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez that he’s trying to make the most of his playing time.
“I never take it for granted,” he said. “I feel like every opportunity we have to take this field is really special especially after what happened the last couple of years, not just to me but to the organization and the city.”
It is possible, though, that Rojas isn’t quite done.
He has flirted with the idea of coming back for another season, something contingent on the Dodgers three-peating, but he notes that’s only his desire.
Even if he changed his mind and wanted to come back, the team could decide to move on.
“I don’t really know when it’s going to be my last time stepping out to home plate and hearing the crowd cheer for me and support me, and that’s the reason why I’m getting a little bit emotional,” he said. “Even though I said I might come back and play if we win the World Series, there’s no guarantee.”
But that’s a worry for later.
For now, Rojas is still focused on the three-peat, and he’s soaking up every second.

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers activate Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki from injured list
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list. Pages missed 27 games after getting hit by a fastball on his left hand on August 21. Sasaki left his start in Atlanta five days later with a blister on his right middle finger. Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Tuesday got a few regulars back as reinforcements heading into the final week of the regular season and into October, activating center fielder Andy Pages and pitcher Roki Sasaki off the injured list.
Pages missed 27 games after getting hit by a fastball on his left hand on August 21. Sasaki left his start in Atlanta five days later with a blister on his right middle finger.
Emmet Sheehan and catcher Eliezer Alfonzo were optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on Monday.
Pages was an All-Star starter this season, and when he got hurt was tied with Yoshinobu Yamamoto for second-highest FanGraphs WAR (3.9) on the team, behind only Shohei Ohtani. By Baseball Reference WAR, Pages is still third on the team now at 5.4, trailing only Ohtani and Yamamoto. That’ll happen with a .272/.338/.458 batting line with a 118 wRC+ combined with plus-defense in center field.
Before getting hit by an errant fastball on August 21, Pages started 125 of the Dodgers’ 129 games, and led the team in plate appearances (550) at the time. Pages and Ohtani are still tied for the Dodgers’ lead with 80 runs batted in. With Pages out, Alek Thomas was first called up to start six games in center field, followed by Tommy Edman starting 17 games, plus three starts by Alex Call and one by Kiké Hernández.
With Edman moving to the outfield and once Thomas was optioned, Miguel Rojas (10) and Alex Freeland (eight) have covered all but one of the starts at second base in September.
Sasaki struggled earlier in the season, but improved as the season progressed. He has a streak of six straight starts with no more than two runs allowed until his blister start in Atlanta. On the season, Sasaki has a 4.46 ERA and 4.42 xERA, but since July 8 he’s down to a 3.25 ERA and 3.76 xERA in eight starts.
With Tarik Skubal, Yoshinobu Yamamoto, and Tyler Glasnow set for the postseason rotation, the Dodgers will see over the next two weeks if Blake Snell will be hampered by his left groin discomfort, and will have Sheehan at the ready. That allows them to use Sasaki in relief, as they did last postseason out of necessity.
“I could see multiples [innings], but it’s not going to be bulk as in four or five innings,” manager Dave Roberts said on Sunday.
Last season was a different situation for Sasaki, who struggled mightily as a starter and spend four months on the injured list before returning in the final week of the regular season. There was no room in the rotation, so he pitched in relief in the postseason. He wasn’t dominant — only six strikeouts among his 43 batters faced, with five walks — but he was effective, allowing only one run over nine appearances and 10 2/3 innings, the highlight his perfect three innings of relief in the Dodgers’ NLDS Game 4 clincher over the Philadelphia Phillies.
Sasaki saved three games last postseason. Roberts said Sasaki probably wouldn’t get an opportunity in a save situation right away this week, but it could progress to that by the postseason.
“I trust Roki in any situation. I would say probably starting a clean inning,” Roberts said. “He’s done it, he’s really good. He’s a neutral pitcher, high-octane stuff. And you really just need four starters. So we’re in a good spot there, for now.”
Sheehan has been fantastic of late, allowing only one run in three starts for the Dodgers over the previous two weeks, with 24 strikeouts in 17 innings. The plan for Sheehan is to start on Saturday for Oklahoma City should the Comets advance to the Triple-A championship game.
Alfonzo was back with the Dodgers since September 6 when Dalton Rushing was placed on the injured list with elbow soreness. In the 14 games since, Alfonzo played only once, pinch-hitting as the designated hitter at the end of a 14-1 blowout of the Cincinnati Reds. He struck out.
Alfonzo made his major league debut against the Padres on July 5, and started nine games behind the plate. He had five hits in 28 at-bats with three doubles and four runs batted in.

item.title: [Sports Spectrum] Mookie Betts, others 'give glory to God' during Dodgers Faith Day
item.dc:creator: Cole Claybourn
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have already clinched their fifth straight National League Division championship and now have their sights set on October, where they hope to become just the third franchise to win three consecutive World Series titles. There’s loads of talent up and down the roster, and there’s also a strong core of believers who are vocal about their faith in God. Six players — utility man Tommy Edman, star outfielder Mookie Betts, reliever Blake Treinen, starting pitcher Justin Wrobles
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have already clinched their fifth straight National League Division championship and now have their sights set on October, where they hope to become just the third franchise to win three consecutive World Series titles. There’s loads of talent up and down the roster, and there’s also a strong core of believers who are vocal about their faith in God.
Six players — utility man Tommy Edman, star outfielder Mookie Betts, reliever Blake Treinen, starting pitcher Justin Wrobleski, reliever Evan Phillips and outfielder Alex Call — joined team chaplain Brandon Cash for Faith and Family Day on Sunday, where they shared their testimonies and how their faith guides them as professional baseball players. It’s an annual event many teams hold, like the Cleveland Guardians and Pittsburgh Pirates.
All six are regular attendees of team chapels and seen as leaders in the clubhouse as much as they are on the field. Call, for example, was traded from the Washington Nationals to L.A. at the trade deadline last season. Cash said he was excited because he heard Call was the spiritual leader in the Washington clubhouse, and he’s since carried that over to the Dodgers.
His testimony mirrored many of his teammates’ in a lot of ways in that he grew up in church with parents who modeled what it looked like to have a strong faith. Like a lot of believers, once he was on his own in college and then as a professional player, he had to decide if his faith was his own or just something he believed because his parents did.
“That’s where it kind of became real for me,” Call said. “I went from, ‘Yeah, I don’t do this or this because I’m a Christian’ to ‘God calls us all to be disciple makers. He calls us all to love and to be a blessing.’ That’s where I turned it up a notch and try not to be ashamed of the Gospel or anything else — just glorify Jesus in my daily life and on the field.”
Wrobleski had a similar upbringing thanks to a mother who set an example and raised him in the faith.
“It’s been a journey for me,” he said. “I’d be lying if I didn’t say there were ups and downs with my faith and God trying to show me things and get me back to where I need to be. Every time I feel like I’ve been down in my life or I feel like things aren’t going the way that I want, it’s just God showing me I need to get back to the Word and pray.”
A first-time All-Star this year, Wrobleski has been a pleasant surprise for the Dodgers and a mainstay in the rotation, making 22 starts with a 3.70 ERA. The Dodgers could use him either in the rotation or as a long reliever in the postseason like last year.
He shared that a verse that’s stuck with him lately is Romans 12:12, which says, “Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, faithful in prayer.”
“That’s something I’m trying to live out right now,” he said. “It’s a journey. Knowing Jesus obviously gives you that peace when you’re out there. For me, it’s big before the game. It’s a super big blessing to pitch for the Dodgers, but there’s a lot of pressure that comes with it. Just knowing that the results aren’t always what matters; it’s just giving your performance to the Lord, good or bad, and that’s kind of been something I’m trying to do this year.”
That pressure is felt by all the players. They know the expectations that come with playing in L.A. They know their team is loaded with talent and high-priced players.
Edman — who shared that his faith grew substantially when he was in college at Stanford thanks to faith mentors and involvement in the Fellowship of Christian Athletes — said he handles the scrutiny of playing pro baseball by remembering that his identity is in Christ.
“As a baseball player, one of the big struggles that we have is our identity being tied up in our performance on the field or being just a baseball player,” Edman said. “Baseball is such a crazy long season and a rollercoaster of emotions that you can go up and down like crazy.
“I have my identity rooted in my role as a son of God and a follower of Jesus Christ. I always have that in my foundation. Not to say that helps me perform on the field, but it definitely allows me to have that inner peace regardless of how I’ve done on the baseball field.”
Tommy Edman talks about his faith journey #dodgers #faith #love Full video: https://t.co/IGEujZWgH9 pic.twitter.com/FM2AM0Mu4H
— RavineQueen1958 (@RavineQueeen) September 21, 2026
Each player has a different background that led them to where they are personally and professionally, and that’s something that makes the chapel dynamic unique, Cash said. For example, Betts didn’t really grow up in the church like some of his teammates did. He spent most of his weekends playing baseball, and going to church just wasn’t much of a priority.
“As I got a little older playing ball, I kind of wanted the sense of purpose, because ball is just an avenue to show what God has given me and given all of us,” said Betts, an eight-time All-Star. “Once I wanted to learn my purpose, I think going to chapel, getting to know Cash, getting to know these guys has really changed my life completely. These are literally like my brothers. Obviously we’ve grown playing baseball and winning together, but I think we’ve grown the most in our Bible studies and our chapels on Sundays.”
He said he just read through 1 and 2 Kings, where he read about King Soloman and how he was wise and felt on top of the world. Betts saw some similarities to pro baseball.
“When you’re on top of the world and everything’s going great, but you lose what’s important, which is God, you kind of lose everything,” he said. “No matter how good or bad I do, I make sure to give glory to God and I make sure that every day I pray and give glory to Him because everything we have here is for Him.”
Mookie Betts talks about his faith #dodgers #Mookie #Betts #faith #love Full video: https://t.co/IGEujZWgH9 pic.twitter.com/7RnFyvHwkN
— RavineQueen1958 (@RavineQueeen) September 21, 2026
Treinen, who’s now in his seventh season with the Dodgers, shared that he sort of begrudgingly attended church growing up. His mother was a member of the worship team, which meant he often spent all morning and part of the afternoon at church when he would’ve rather been home watching football.
“As I’ve gotten older, I’ve greatly appreciated the stubbornness and consistency that my mom put in my life for me and my brother to take us to church on Sunday,” he said. “It was a lot as a kid, but it built a structure of faith and a standard of worship in life.”
He recalled a moment at a youth conference at the University of Tennessee where he said he “felt the tangible presence of the Holy Spirit just rock me and put me in my seat.” He recounted how Christians should always be able to give an answer for the hope they have in Jesus, and that experience is what he goes back to when explaining where he first believed.
“We all have the right to believe what we want,” he said. “But when you see the truth and the facts and the tangible hand of God in your life, it separates just wanting to be a good person and knowing Jesus is real, to ‘this is absolute.’ I’ve experienced the presence of the Father and I will forever with my life.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers activated Andy Pages from the 10-day injured list and optioned Eliezer Alfonzo to Triple-A Oklahoma City. The move was made during the off day on Monday, but the Dodgers did not officially announce it at the time.
In addition, Roki Sasaki was also activated while Emmet Sheehan was optioned.
The Dodgers first recalled Alfonzo when Dalton Rushing was placed on the IL on Sept. 6. During his second stint with the club, Alfonzo only received one at-bat, which came against the Cincinnati Reds on Sept. 9 when he struck out.
Alfonzo was the third catcher on the roster, which Dodgers manager Dave Roberts explained was to allow the club to more freely use Will Smith and Hunter Feduccia as pinch-hitters when they didn’t start.
The Dodgers also did not need to make a 40-man roster move to call up Alfonzo, which likely played into their decision.
The 26-year-old has appeared in 13 total games this season, making his MLB debut and batting .179/.179/.250 with four RBI and three runs scored in 28 plate appearances. In Oklahoma City, he was hitting .302/.378/.409 in 256 plate appearances.
Pages is back with the Dodgers for the first time in a month after he landed on the IL with a left hand fracture on Aug. 22.
Pages suffered the injury when he was hit by a pitch from Pittsburgh Pirates starter Bubba Chandler. The 26-year-old underwent surgery shortly after to insert a compression screw in his hand to speed up the healing process.
Pages did not go on a rehab assignment before returning, but did workouts at Dodger Stadium, which included hitting on the field, running the bases, and doing outfield drills.
That makes this stretch of six games important for Pages to face live pitching and get as many at-bats as possible to prepare for the postseason. But even with that in mind, the Dodgers also have to be cautious about building him back up and not overworking him after a month of not playing.
“So we have obviously, assuming he gets back on Tuesday, then there’s six in a row, and that seems pretty aggressive,” Roberts explained.
“So I think that we do want to get him as many at-bats as possible, but we have to make sure that his legs are under him, feeling good, so we don’t go backward or get injured in that respect. So it is going to be a balancing act, and just keeping a keen eye on Andy for sure.”
Pages is batting .272/.338/.458 with 25 doubles, 21 home runs, 80 RBI and 72 runs scored this season. He has also been among the top defensive players in MLB.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] What Andy Pages means to Dodgers’ postseason after returning from injury
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris

item.content:encoded:
In too many cases this year, the Dodgers dealt with injuries to players that lasted far longer than they initially anticipated.
On Tuesday, however, they got one of their most important bats back right on schedule.
The Dodgers have officially activated center fielder Andy Pages, according to MLB's transactions log, adding him back into their lineup for the final week of the regular season.
Pages had been out one month, after going on the injured list on Aug. 22 with a hand fracture he suffered from a 100 mph hit-by-pitch. His initial timeline of 4-5 weeks proved accurate, thanks in part to a surgical procedure he underwent to accelerate his recovery process.
The question now is whether Pages will be able to recapture his All-Star form offensively following such a significant injury.
Manager Dave Roberts acknowledged that challenge over the week, saying that while he is still "expecting good at-bats" from the third-year slugger, he was still "waiting just like you guys are waiting to see how it looks."
For many hitters, a broken hand can cause a lack of feel or strength in their swings. The last Dodgers player to endure such an injury was Mookie Betts in 2024, when he went from an MVP candidate beforehand to a below-league-average hitter for not only the rest of that year but 2025, as well.
However, the Dodgers are hopeful in what Pages will be able to provide the rest of the season –– not only with his bat but also his premium glove (and arm) in center field.
This year, Pages leads all MLB outfielders with 13 assists and ranks second among center fielders with 20 defensive runs saved. That alone, Roberts said, is "a big reason why he's still a valuable player, even coming off the IL with the uncertainty of the offense."
As for his offense, the manager added: "We'll still bet on [that, too]."
Pages was in the midst of a career-best season before getting hurt, batting .272 with 21 home runs, 80 RBIs, a .797 OPS and 45 walks (a sharp increase from the 29 he drew in each of his first two big-league campaigns). It was good enough to help him earn a first selection to the Midsummer Classic and a bump up to the No. 2 spot in the Dodgers' batting order.
The 25-year-old had cooled off in the second half, after finishing May batting .294 with 13 long balls. He also didn't get a typical recovery process as a hitter during his time on the IL, unable to go on a minor-league rehab assignment (since the minor-league season was ending as he returned to health) or even face pitching in a live batting session.
Instead, he went through simulated games last week in which he alternated between hitting off a machine at Dodger Stadium and taking reps in center field on balls hit by members of the coaching staff.
Still, the Dodgers are confident he will be able to provide enough all-around production in his return to the active roster now.
"Playing a premium position and playing it well," Roberts said, "is hugely important."

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers top prospect Jose De Paula was surprised to see Shohei Ohtani in the dugout during Friday's game against the San Francisco Giants.
His face made that clear.
De Paula said he didn't expect Ohtani to be in the dugout when he embraced his teammates after scoring a run for the Dodgers in the contest, leading to his viral reaction.
“I actually seen him earlier that day but I wasn’t expecting him to be at the game," De Paula said.
"He caught me by surprise, I was giving everybody a handshake, I gave him a handshake, but then I double take like he’s here.”
De Paula made his MLB debut on Sept. 11 after the Dodgers placed Ohtani on the injured list due to a variety of injuries he's been battling.
The 21-year-old is Ohtani's replacement in the lineup and serves as the Dodgers' designated hitter for now.
De Paula also mentioned that he is excited to see Ohtani back at the plate for the Dodgers.
“I can’t wait until he’s back. To see what he does in the box, you don’t see that every day so I can’t wait," he said.
In 28 at-bats as a Dodger, De Paula has recorded a .268 batting average with a .974 OPS, one home run, seven RBIs and one stolen base.
How Close Is Shohei Ohtani to Returning?
It hasn't been a pretty second half for Ohtani, as he battled with injuries for the better part of a month-plus.
Since the start of August, Ohtani's bat has gone ice cold.
From Aug. 1 until he was placed on the 15-day IL, Ohtani has a .231 batting average with 27 hits, six home runs, 13 RBIs and 19 runs.
While Ohtani's numbers are far below what is expected, the Dodgers hope that is a thing of the past.
Ohtani is eligible to return to the lineup Wednesday, and he's progressing well in his recovery. The 32-year-old took a major step this past weekend, as he was seen running the bases and hitting off the Trajekt machine.
Manager Dave Roberts said he hopes Ohtani will be ready to return Wednesday. If not, the four-time MVP could make his return Thursday.
Ohtani is in his third year with the Dodgers after signing a 10-year, $700 million contract in December 2023.
The two-way superstar has led the Dodgers to back-to-back World Series titles. While he isn't at 100% with the postseason nearing, he's expected to do his part to try to lead Los Angeles to yet another World Series title in 2026.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Shohei Ohtani Has 'Good Chance' of Returning to Dodgers This Week
item.dc:creator: Cameron Kiszla

item.content:encoded:
It’s been weeks since Los Angeles Dodgers fans have seen a healthy and productive Shohei Ohtani in the lineup, but that wait could be nearly over.
Ohtani could be activated as soon as Wednesday, reports Sonja Chen of MLB.com.
That means Ohtani is likely to be playing in a couple of the games against the San Diego Padres in the last regular season home series of the season.
“There’s a good chance next series we’ll see him,” manager Dave Roberts said.
Why hasn’t Shohei Ohtani been playing?
Ohtani has been dealing with multiple injuries, including to his knee and his bicep.
Those injuries already shut down his pitching earlier this season, but even with a change to pitching-only duties, Ohtani was clearly suffering from something.
Ohtani had a four-hit game on Aug. 17, which included two home runs, and then his batting statistics fell off a cliff.
In the 14 games he’s played since that performance against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field, Ohtani is hitting .130/.288/.241/.529, per Baseball Reference.
He has seven hits, including a double, a triple and a homer, but has also struck out 22 times.
Compare that to his overall season slash line of .277/.380/.522/.902, statistics that are much more in line with his reputation as one of the best baseball players of all time.
What will Shohei Ohtani be like when he returns to the Dodgers?
It’s worth noting that Ohtani, even with this 15-day stint on the injured list, won’t come back fully healed.
Chen said, though, that what was pain is now “discomfort.”
That sounds like Ohtani still won’t be 100%, but Ohtani at even 90% would be a perennial All-Star and could absolutely change the team’s fortunes in the playoffs.
We’ll know more for sure once Ohtani is back, as he’ll likely get a lot of playing time, Roberts said.
“If Ohtani returns when he is eligible on Wednesday, he will have only five regular-season games to reacclimate himself to big league action before the postseason,” Chen wrote. “Roberts said he plans to play Ohtani in every game once he returns because he will need the live at-bats.”
Once he does return, Roberts expects Ohtani to be much closer to his MVP form than he was for that rough stretch of August.
“I do think that when he’s activated,” Roberts said, “it’s going to be the best physical place he’s been in in quite some time.”
Do you think Shohei Ohtani will be back to playing like himself when he returns to the Dodgers this week?

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are pacing toward having a first-round bye, avoiding the NL Wild Card round, and it would seem they are getting healthy at just the right time. The expectation in recent weeks was that Shohei Ohtani, Andy Pages, and Roki Sasaki would return before the end of the regular season, and the Dodgers quietly revealed the roster moves to map everything out.
Updating their transaction log overnight, the Dodgers have reinstated Pages and Sasaki from the IL, and optioned Emmet Sheehan and Eliezer Alfonzo to the minors. With Ohtani eligible to be reinstated from the IL on Wednesday, the expectation is that Alex Freeland will be the corresponding move.
For Ohtani and Pages, the goal was simply having them back before the start of the playoffs. They now have a runway to shake off the rust over these next handful of games, before likely having next week off before playing in the NLDS.
Circumstances are a little more dire for Sasaki, who hasn't secured a spot on LA's playoff roster. Dave Roberts has already confirmed that Sasaki will be used out of the bullpen upon his return, and it goes to one of the biggest questions facing the Dodgers ahead of the playoffs.
The Dodgers are getting healthy just in time, but there are still answers needed
The Dodgers need to find answers in the bullpen. Ironically, the stage is set for Sasaki to repeat a similar shift he made last season. While the Dodgers have been adamant that Sasaki's future is as a starting pitcher, he was used as a quasi-finisher during the playoffs last year, and thrived.
Considering the questions surrounding Edwin Diaz and Edgardo Henriquez currently dealing with an injury, Sasaki once again becoming an effective high-leverage option for the Dodgers would be a major development for the playoffs.
The story of the Dodgers since the trade deadline has been that they are leaking oil. Sure, they traded for Tarik Skubal, but the operation looked faulty. With the returns of Sasaki, Pages, and Ohtani likely on Wednesday, they are finally reaching a level of healthy they haven't had for most of the season.
In other words, despite how uneven things have looked, the Dodgers are once again in a position to do whay they do best and flip the swith on during the month of October.

item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball's postseason rapidly is approaching, with the Los Angeles Dodgers seeking a third straight World Series title. It remains to be seen how much some of the game's biggest stars will be able to participate in the playoffs, though.
The Dodgers are once again among the best teams in the big leagues, and they'll have several challengers in October, including the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays. All three teams could finish the regular season with 100 wins or more. Los Angeles is rolling even though four-time MVP Shohei Ohtani's health is a concern.
The New York Yankees, Boston Red Sox and Atlanta Braves also have clinched spots in the postseason. Yankees slugger Aaron Judge, a three-time AL MVP, is dealing with a right calf strain that will keep him on the injured list until at least the final day of the regular season.
While the 12-team playoff field appears mostly set, there are a few long-shot contenders for the postseason, and specific matchups are in flux.
Here's some of what to watch as the season comes to a close.
AL race is murky while NL is more defined
There's quite a bit of mediocrity in the AL Central and West divisions this season, which has led to some fascinating pennant races and could lead to a sub-.500 team making the postseason.
The Cleveland Guardians (81-75) have a narrow advantage over the Chicago White Sox (80-76) in the AL Central while the Texas Rangers (78-78) are just ahead of the Houston Astros (77-79) in the AL West.
Over in the National League, the playoff bracket is close to set.
The Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) and Philadelphia Phillies (86-70) are jockeying for position in the wild-card race but almost certainly will make the postseason. The only team within shouting distance is the Arizona Diamondbacks (82-74), who are four games back.
MVP races, stats to watch
MLB's major awards probably won't have much drama this season.
Both MVP races have strong favorites with Chicago's Pete Crow-Armstrong running away with the NL honor while Houston's Yordan Alvarez is the probable choice in the AL, though Tampa Bay's Junior Caminero also has had a fantastic season. Alvarez still has a shot at a rare Triple Crown. He leads the AL in batting average at .313 but his 40 homers are one behind Caminero and his 99 RBIs are nine back of Baltimore's Pete Alonso.
For the Cy Young Award, Milwaukee flame thrower Jacob Misiorowski and New York ace Cam Schlittler are the favorites in the NL and AL, respectively.
The Rookie of the Year races also look set with Cincinnati's Sal Stewart and his 110-RBI season the leader in the NL and Detroit's Kevin McGonigle the favorite in the AL.
What is the MLB playoff format?
There are 12 teams that qualify for MLB's postseason, including six teams from both the AL and NL. The three division winners in each league get seeds No. 1 through No. 3, ranked by win-loss record. Then the three wild-card teams get seeds No. 4 through No. 6, also ranked by win-loss record.
The top two teams with the best record in both the AL and NL automatically advance to the Division Series. The other eight teams play in the Wild Card Series, which is a best-of-three format beginning on Tuesday, Sept. 30. In both the AL and NL, the No. 6 seed will travel to face the No. 3 seed while the No. 5 seed goes to No. 4. The higher seed hosts all three games.
The winners then advance to the best-of-five Division Series, followed by the best-of-seven League Championship Series and a best-of-seven World Series between the winners of the AL and NL.
What is the MLB postseason schedule?
Wild Card Round: Sept. 29-Oct. 1 (NBC/Peacock)
Division Series: Oct. 3-10 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
Championship Series: Oct. 11-20 (AL on TBS, NL on FOX/FS1)
World Series: Oct. 23-31 (FOX)
Who are the favorites to win the World Series?
The Dodgers (+220) are the favorites to capture a third straight World Series title while the Brewers (+600), Yankees (+800) and Rays (+800) are viewed as the top contenders.

item.content:encoded:
Unless the Los Angeles Angels win their final six games and somehow figure out how to get Major League Baseball to overturn the results of 15 others, the club will finish below the .500 mark for the 11th consecutive season. This postseason will mark the 12th in a row to not feature any Halos, and it has been 17 years since the last time they won a game in the playoffs. The Arte Moreno era is ending, with Los Angeles Rams owner Stan Kroenke taking over the helm. And while Kroenke has a mixed record as an owner, a mixed record would qualify as progress after Moreno. New ownership tends to represent a new beginning for a team, setting up an important question: Can the Angels return to playing October baseball in the near future? After all, while the team doesn’t have the same revenue as the Dodgers, it’s still located in the second-most-populous metropolitan area in the United States; theoretically, they have the resources to speed up the process.
I like to joke about baseball’s Anna Karenina issue, because I think the novel’s first line — “Happy families are all alike; every unhappy family is unhappy in its own way” — is an even more appropriate observation for baseball teams than it is for families. All great baseball teams look kind of the same, but every lousy team looks different. As bad teams go, the Angels have never been spectacularly lousy; if they fail to at least split their last six games, 2026 will be the first time ever that the franchise has lost 100 games. Still, this is a franchise that hasn’t figured out how to play .500 ball while employing the best player of the 2010s and the likely best player of the 2020s. They even had both of those guys on the team for a while! That the Angels have tended to hover just below mediocre rather than being hilariously awful is probably one of the reasons they’ve never truly blown things up and tried something radically different. The Angels never reached a point where they just threw stuff against the wall to see what sticks, something the White Sox finally accepted a few years ago, and that the Rockies appear to be starting to accept now.
If the Angels were to compete again soon, where would the talent come from? At first blush, there’s no amount of squinting that can make the Angels look like they have the foundation of a solid team. Mike Trout is still pretty good, but he’s a galaxy away from the player he once was, and as hard as it is to believe, he turned 35 last month. Zach Neto is solid, but if you listed the rest of the starting lineup and told me that I was looking at the starting lineup for the Durham Bulls or the Round Rock Express, I might believe you.
To get a more comprehensive look at the team’s offensive future, I ran updated WAR and OPS+ projections for the Angels over the next five seasons. I’ve included pretty much everyone on the roster or in the high minors, as well as those top prospects who are at a minor league level where projections are practical. That leaves out intriguing players like Johnny Slawinski, Joswa Lugo, and Yilver De Paula, but we’re also talking about non-elite prospects at the very low levels, so the median outlook for their projections is going to be fairly low. Still, it’s worth keeping in mind that there are at least a few additional lottery tickets out there for the Angels.
To make a quick read of the table easier, I’ve highlighted all of the 3-WAR projected seasons in red and all of the 2-WAR projected seasons in yellow. I’ve also blacked out the seasons where a player isn’t under team control, or where ZiPS is highly confident that they won’t be in baseball based on their performance. Oh, and I threw in Anthony Rendon for the sake of curiosity:

There… isn’t a lot of color in that chart. ZiPS doesn’t see anyone beyond Neto as a key part of a contending team. Trout is almost certainly going to become less and less of a contributor in coming seasons, and Denzer Guzman and Christian Moore look more like complementary options than guys threatening to attend a string of All-Star games (though Guzman does have some decent projected upside). Even given the very real possibility that ZiPS is underrating Arjun Nimmala, that’s still a stunning lack of offensive talent in the organization.
Let’s move on to the pitching, where things do look a bit better. There are no borderline star seasons projected, so I’ve highlighted all the 100 ERA+ seasons in yellow:

Reid Detmers and Walbert Ureña both project as very good mid-rotation starters, and the latter is a long way from free agency. There may be No Such Thing as a Pitching Prospect©, but ZiPS does think Tyler Bremner is likely to be at least solid. None of the rest of the arms look amazing, but the Angels do have an interesting bunch of plausible bullpen candidates, though nobody who would blow your mind. If the Angels get lucky with either Grayson Rodriguez or George Klassen, and Najer Victor figures out the significance of that white house-shaped pentagon next to the batter, it’s a pitching staff they could make quite decent with a few splashy upgrades.
Sum it all up, and ZiPS sees the Angels as a 70-win team in 2027, with only minor growth from there based on their in-organization options. To that end, the team’s player development absolutely has to improve; the Angels only barely moved out of the bottom third of our farm rankings on the last update, the first time they’ve done so since 2020. That’s particularly concerning for a team that hasn’t contended in more than a decade. Hopefully the team will move on from a draft philosophy that emphasizes high-floor/low-ceiling prospects who can be promoted to the majors very quickly.
As for their options beyond the organization, could the Angels contend with a spending spree next year? I get asked that question fairly regularly in my weekly chats, so at least someone is interested in the answer, or at least wants to trick me into writing about the Angels. Let’s give it a spin.
A contending Angels team needs a high-end starting pitcher, a veteran bulk arm, and probably three additional good relievers. Here’s one set of potential additions:

Most of the names here are interchangeable with other options, but you can’t really fake signing Tarik Skubal and have to go with the real thing. ZiPS estimates that doing so would make the Angels a 77-85 team, but also one that just added more than $80 million in salary to get there.
As for the offense, it needs a lot of work and there is only so much they can practically do, even in an ultra-aggressive buying frenzy. Assuming that Trout stays at DH, they certainly need a couple of outfielders, and there’s no Aaron Judge to sign. The corner infield spots aren’t the weakest on the roster, but Teruaki Sato is one of the best players (possibly) available, and I’d like a bit more certainty at second base if we’re doing full-on win-now mode:

You may have noted the problem I’m running into for the quick-fix route: There’s a hard limit on just how many difference-makers there are available in free agency. These four signings probably add another $80 million to the payroll, and once you throw in the player benefits, the Angels would have a luxury tax payroll creeping into the $300 million range. Their projection would only improve to 83-79, and while that would be the team’s best year in a decade, it’s a pretty brutal projection to intentionally pay $300 million for.
In the end, the Angels don’t appear to have enough in-house options to make buying their way into contention a real possibility. That means that the road ahead will be a lot harder, with them eating some awful seasons without any pretense of contending, trying some new things, and taking some chances, all of which the franchise has struggled with for the last decade. As it turns out, needing to replace about 20 players on your roster isn’t something you can do quickly. By the time the Angels are good again, we might be talking about the next lockout!
Dan Szymborski is a senior writer for FanGraphs and the developer of the ZiPS projection system. He was a writer for ESPN.com from 2010-2018, a regular guest on a number of radio shows and podcasts, and a voting BBWAA member. He also maintains a terrible Twitter account at @DSzymborski.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] This Day In Dodgers History: Duke Snider, Don Sutton, Fernando Valenzuela, Home Run Record & Jaime Jarrín
item.dc:creator: Staff Writer

item.content:encoded:
Sept. 22 is a notable date in Los Angeles Dodgers franchise history for multiple reasons, and also for the 1957 Brooklyn team because of Duke Snider.
On the final day of the regular season that year, Snider slugged two home runs in a 7-3 win against the Philadelphia Phillies. That gave Snider a fifth consecutive season with at least 40 homers, which tied Ralph Kiner’s National League record.
That wound up being Snider’s last prolific power season as he never surpassed 23 homers for the remainder of his career, which ended with the San Francisco Giants in 1964.
Beginning with Brooklyn in 1947, Snider played 16 seasons with the Dodgers organization. He earned seven consecutive All-Star Game selections during that span and finished in the top-10 in NL MVP voting in five of those seasons.
Dodgers history: Sept. 22
Sutton reaches 20 wins
On Sept. 22, 1976, Don Sutton threw a complete game against the San Francisco Giants at Candlestick Park to earn his 20th win of the season. He tacked on another victory that year but it wound up being the Hall of Famer’s first and only season reaching 20 wins.
Sutton passed away in January 2021 and was among those honored during the Hall of Fame ceremony this year.
Valenzuela makes history as Mexican pitcher
Ten years after Sutton reached 20 wins, Fernando Valenzuela accomplished the same feat by holding the Houston Astros to just two hits in a Dodgers’ 9-2 victory at the Astrodome. Valenzuela became the first Mexican pitcher to win 20 games in a single season.
Dodgers franchise home run record
After setting a franchise record with 221 home runs during the 2017 season, the Dodgers broke that mark on Sept. 22, 2018, when Yasmani Grandal slugged the team’s 222nd long ball in the sixth inning of a 7-2 win over the San Diego Padres.
The Dodgers finished with 235 home runs that season, then shattered it to set a new franchise high and NL record with 279 in 2019.
Jarrín immortalized at Dodger Stadium
On Sept. 22, 2019, the Dodgers held a pregame ceremony to induct Spanish-language broadcaster Jaime Jarrín into the Dodger Stadium Ring of Honor.
Pepe Yñiguez, Fernando Valenzuela and Hall-of-Fame broadcaster Vin Scully were among those to speak during the festivities.
Jarrí became the 12th person inducted into the Ring of Honor, joining Scully, Pee Wee Reese, Tommy Lasorda, Snider, Jim Gilliam, Sutton, Walter Alston, Sandy Koufax, Roy Campanella, Jackie Robinson and Don Drysdale.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers right-handed pitcher Emmet Sheehan sent a message to the team ahead of the postseason with his role on the team still uncertain.
Sheehan went to the minors at the beginning of August following the arrival of Tarik Skubal and a string of poor results on his part. Prior to his stint in the minors, Sheehan had a 5.29 ERA and had just allowed five earned runs in just 2.2 innings pitched.
How Long Was Emmet Sheehan in the Minors?
He managed to get right in the minors, though, allowing just three earned runs over the course of 18 innings pitched in Triple-A. He returned in the middle of September, and has three starts under his belt since returning.
In those appearances, Sheehan has a 0.53 ERA over the course of 17 innings pitched, striking out 24 batters. He pitched Sunday, striking out nine batters through 5.1 scoreless innings of relief, during which he only allowed one hit and one walk. On the year, Sheehan now has a 4.57 ERA through 112.1 innings pitched, striking out 132 batters during his time in MLB.
The Dodgers are optioning him back to Triple-A to keep their bullpen fresh throughout the remainder of the season as they look to secure the No. 2 seed in the NL, but he can still feature in the postseason and is willing to do whatever it takes to help the team.
“I feel like I’m in a much better spot now,” Sheehan told Dodgers Nation’s Noel Sanchez and reporters. “Whatever role they want me to do going forward, I’m ready to do it. It was nice to get that experience coming out of the pen, and I’m ready to go.”
What Role Would Emmet Sheehan Have in the Postseason?
Sheehan has predominantly played as a starter for the Dodgers this season, making his first relief appearance of the year on Sunday, but would almost definitely stay in the bullpen if he makes the roster come October.
The Dodgers have a four-man rotation planned out already, as Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Skubal are all healthy and likely to be the Dodgers’ starters during the postseason.
Sheehan would fit in the bullpen as a long relief arm, and would likely be the Dodgers’ go-to man in those scenarios.
Landon Knack and Bobby Miller have taken on those responsibilities as of late, but Sheehan’s recent results should qualify him for a spot over both Knack and Miller.
Will the Dodgers Bring Emmet Sheehan to the Postseason?
The Dodgers are allowed a maximum of 13 pitchers on their roster for the postseason, and Sheehan will almost certainly be included in those options due to his ability to pitch out of the bullpen.
Sheehan came out of the bullpen for the Dodgers during last year’s postseason, and while he wasn’t the most effective in that role, his recent surge and experience in that area will be key for LA as they look to win a third consecutive World Series.
The right-hander won’t pitch again for the Dodgers in the regular season due to the minimum 15-day stay in the minors, so unless the Dodgers need to recall him due to an injury, he’ll hope the impression he made during his strong September is enough to warrant a spot on the postseason roster.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Josue De Paula Named 2026 Texas League Player Of The Year
item.dc:creator: Matthew Moreno
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers prospect Josue De Paula was named Texas League Player of the Year for the 2026 Minor League season. De Paula was among six members of the Drillers organization to receive honors. Eric Wedge was named Texas League Manager of the Year, while De Paula, Mike Sirota, Zyhir Hope, Jake Gelof and Nick Robertson were all selected to the All-Star team as well. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers prospect Josue De Paula was named Texas League Player of the Year for the 2026 Minor League season. De Paula was among six members of the Drillers organization to receive honors.
Eric Wedge was named Texas League Manager of the Year, while De Paula, Mike Sirota, Zyhir Hope, Jake Gelof and Nick Robertson were all selected to the All-Star team as well. Of course, Hope’s time with the Drillers came to an end at the deadline as he was included in the trade package sent to the Detroit Tigers for Tarik Skubal.
Less than a week after the trade, Hope was named Texas League Player of the Month for July.
Josue De Paula’s Texas League award
De Paula is the fourth Drillers player to be named the Texas League’s MVP, joining Bubba Smith (1996), Ryan Shealy (2004) and Matt Beaty (2017).
The 21-year-old appeared in four games for Tulsa at the end of last season and spent all of this year with the Dodgers’ affiliate before getting called up to make his MLB debut. De Paula became the first Dodgers position player to get promoted directly from Double-A during president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman’s tenure.
While appearing in 124 games for the Drillers, De Paula batted .303/.401/.547 with 37 doubles, two triples, 27 home runs, 104 RBI and 31 stolen bases. He led all Texas League players in total hits (152), RBI and runs scored (106), and was tied for most doubles.
De Paula additionally set career highs in games played, doubles, home runs and RBI. He additionally was one stolen base shy of equaling his most in any Minor League season and three walks shy of tying a career-best mark.
With his RBI and runs scored totals, De Paula joined Carlos Pena as the only players in Drillers franchise history to have at least 100 in both categories in the same season.
De Paula’s impressive offensive success has carried over with the Dodgers, with remarkable plate discipline translating to quality and productive at-bats.
De Paula has garnered praise from Dodgers manager Dave Roberts and teammates alike, and seemingly played his way into the discussion for a potential postseason roster spot. De Paula also has already made Dodgers franchise history as their first player to ever wear No. 95.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers notes: Is this team (and Edwin Diaz) playoff ready?
item.dc:creator: Andy Lane Chapman
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers have managed to work their way out of their usual late summer lull, by going 14-5 so far in the month of September. But they face a test starting Tuesday to see if they really are in postseason form. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have managed to work their way out of their usual late summer lull, by going 14-5 so far in the month of September. But they face a test starting Tuesday to see if they really are in postseason form.
This month, the Dodgers have beat up on below .500 teams in the Washington Nationals, Cincinnati Reds, and San Francisco Giants. But they have one last team with a winning record to face before the playoffs – the San Diego Padres.
The Padres come in to this series winners of 13 of their last 14 games, needing two wins to secure a wildcard playoff spot. They have never made the playoffs three seasons in a row in the history of their franchise.
"I feel like the whole team is in a good spot right now," San Diego's Fernando Tatis Jr. told the San Diego Union-Tribune on Sunday. "We're playing really good baseball. We're checking in when we have to. The entire lineup is in a good spot right now. So when it's going like that, it's … a good time."
For their part, the Dodgers have a magic number of three to secure the second bye in the playoffs, which is important in setting the rotation that the Dodgers want.
"I think it's going to be a good kind of (playoff) primer," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the upcoming series. "They're a very talented team. They're playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I'm looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys."
Andy Pages is expected to be activated off the IL on Tuesday, hopefully fully healed and ready to add to the Dodgers offensive firepower.
Doug Padilla of the OC Register covers more of the details of what the Dodgers are thinking in their last six games of the season here.
One of the things still up in the air as far as the postseason roster goes is the status of Edwin Diaz, and if he can make a positive impact in the playoffs.
Diaz returned from the IL on Friday, a has two scoreless outings. But is that enough to get back on Dave Roberts' trust tree?
"It's been really disappointing," Díaz said of his season. "But now I've found growth to come back and perform the way everyone was expecting."
Diaz was on the IL earlier this season after having surgery on bone chips in his elbow and he came back ready to return to the leverage part of the bullpen. Except he wasn't actually ready.
Katie Woo of The Athletic covers all of the ins and outs of Diaz's return and playoff roster hopes here:
"Everybody was telling me I have a new elbow, so just keep going, keep climbing the ladder," Díaz said. "You will be fine. We trust you. They always stayed positive with me, and you know, I was positive too. I know when I'm right, I can do really good things. I just trusted the process with them. They stuck with me. They supported me. So I was OK."
But he wasn't ok. In his nine outings after returning from the IL, Diaz's ERA swelled to 11.85. He landed back on the IL with neck inflammation. So far in this return, he seems to be doing better. But with only six games left, he only has three to four games to prove he's playoff ready.

item.content:encoded:
SANTO DOMINGO, RD (Nelson de la Rosa–Prensa CBPC).- El 22 de septiembre de 1986, Fernando Valenzuela volvió a colocar su nombre en la historia del béisbol mexicano al alcanzar una cifra que hasta entonces ningún lanzador nacido en ese país había conseguido en las Grandes Ligas.
Hace exactamente 40 años, el zurdo de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles derrotó 9-2 a los Astros de Houston en el Astrodome para convertirse en el primer pitcher mexicano con 20 victorias en una temporada de MLB.
Valenzuela recorrió las nueve entradas, permitió solamente dos imparables y dos carreras —una limpia—, concedió tres boletos y ponchó a cinco. Incluso colaboró a la ofensiva con un sencillo productor.
Terminó aquella temporada con récord de 21-11 y efectividad de 3.14, completando 20 de sus 34 aperturas. Tal resultado lo mantuvo en la lucha por el Premio Cy Young de la Lia Nacional, donde finalmente terminó en el segundo lugar.
Pero la historia de Fernando no se limitó a las Grandes Ligas. La Serie del Caribe también formó parte de su extraordinaria trayectoria.
Cuatro años antes de aquella victoria número 20, Valenzuela había regresado a México convertido ya en una de las grandes figuras del béisbol. Venía de una inolvidable temporada de 1981 con los Dodgers, en la que conquistó el Premio Cy Young, el Novato del Año y la Serie Mundial.
En febrero de 1982 reforzó a los Naranjeros de Hermosillo en la Serie del Caribe celebrada precisamente en esa ciudad. Y allí protagonizó una de sus actuaciones más recordadas en el clásico regional.
Frente a los Leones de Ponce de Puerto Rico retiró a los primeros 17 bateadores que enfrentó y mantuvo el juego sin imparables hasta el octavo episodio en una victoria mexicana 14-0. MLB recoge aquella actuación al repasar la trayectoria caribeña del zurdo.
Valenzuela disputó tres Series del Caribe: en 1982 y 2001 con los Naranjeros de Hermosillo y en 1993 como refuerzo de los Venados de Mazatlán. En sus tres participaciones terminó invicto, con marca de 1-0 y efectividad de 1.05.
Su última aparición resulta particularmente significativa. En Culiacán 2001, con 40 años, “El Toro” volvió a vestir el uniforme de Hermosillo en el torneo regional, casi dos décadas después de aquella primera participación de 1982.
La huella que dejó en el clásico caribeño recibió posteriormente uno de sus mayores reconocimientos: en 2013 Fernando Valenzuela fue exaltado al Salón de la Fama de la Serie del Caribe, junto a figuras como Ricardo Carty, Tony Peña y Candy Maldonado.
Cuarenta años después, aquel triunfo número 20 en la MLB permanece como otra de las grandes fechas de una carrera que dejó huella a ambos lados de la frontera y también en la historia del béisbol caribeño.
Fotos: Getty Images /Archivo CBPC

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] The Dodgers’ Josue De Paula can hit. Now he’s out to prove he can play defense, too
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula sat down with third base and outfield coach Dino Ebel in the visiting coach’s room at Great American Ball Park. Ebel pulled up defensive metrics on three different outfielders. One was Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite and MLB’s defensive fWAR leader. Another was Dodgers center fielder Andy Pages, who has evolved into an elite center fielder during his time with the organization.
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
Dodgers rookie Josue De Paula sat down with third base and outfield coach Dino Ebel in the visiting coach’s room at Great American Ball Park. Ebel pulled up defensive metrics on three different outfielders.
One was Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong, the National League MVP favorite and MLB’s defensive fWAR leader. Another was Dodgers center fielder Andy Pages, who has evolved into an elite center fielder during his time with the organization. And the third was De Paula.
“There’s a lot of colors in the game, and when you have red, it’s not good, and when you have green, it’s good,” Ebel said in a recent conversation with The Times. “And he saw a lot of green from the other two players, and he saw some green and some red on his side. So it kind of hit home with him.”
The reports broke down his first step, going right and left, arm strength, and so on.
For the past 17 years, Chaz Perea and his four-person crew have been responsible for every bit of stadium landscaping that isn’t the field itself.
“Just comparing [Pages’] journey, too, with mine — and that it’s possible,” De Paula said of what he took from the conversation. “I have all the tools under my belt to be able to do so. It’s more about just being focused throughout the whole thing, and having that drive to want to do it.
“And when I saw it, it was also a motivation for me. It was like, all right, let’s go now.”
It was De Paula’s bat that earned him a call-up when Shohei Ohtani landed on the injured list. And it’s his bat that’s now making his case for a postseason roster spot. (“This is more of a trial run,” manager Dave Roberts said last week.)
For De Paula to stick in the majors, however, his development on the defensive side is going to be key. As he has risen through the system, his outfield play has lagged behind his offensive influence. But the Dodgers have already seen growth this year.
“Our goal is to become, one day, a Gold Glover,” Ebel said. “And I think he’s young enough to do it, and his mindset is right, he’s got a chance to do that.”
Dodgers special assistant Jason Heyward started poring over video of the team’s top prospects — a group chalk full of outfielders, led by De Paula — as soon as he began working for the Dodgers’ front office at the beginning of May.
“He handles constructive criticism, for me, with some of the best of them that I’ve been around,” Heyward said.
Heyward, a five-time Gold Glove outfielder, first met De Paula in spring training in 2024, when the prospect jumped in on outfield drills with the major leaguers. In Heyward’s new role, he’s made multiple trips to Tulsa, Okla., to work with De Paula and the rest of the group there.
Heyward emphasized building a consistent and productive routine.
“He makes it so easy to have something to make relatable to this because I’ve seen his work in the cage, I’ve seen his attention to detail,” Heyward said. “He takes on challenges, but it’s not a, ‘Let me hurry up and get to this challenge, let me rush through this.’ He’s like, ‘No, I’m going to go about this how I want to go about it, I’m not going to be rushed, I’m going to lock in, and I’m going to give this like all my focus.’”
That process on the offensive side was something Heyward encouraged De Paula to tap into in all parts of his game, including defense. But De Paula said Heyward also acknowledged that the nature of playing in the outfield can make that more difficult.
“Hitting, you are always unfocused on the next pitch, your mind is always going,” De Paula said. “But you could go three days without getting a fly ball. So it’s kind of easy for your mind to drift and stuff like that. But it’s just more about tips of engagement and that intensity of focus.”
Heyward was a fitting person to deliver the message. Once a heralded prospect for the Braves, he put together a 16-year MLB career that included a second-place rookie of the year finish, an All-Star nod, and a stellar reputation for defense and veteran leadership.
“It’s a blessing to have somebody like that in your corner, especially rooting for you, to be able to see your talent, like what you’re capable of,” De Paula said. “He’s been through it, so he knows, man. So it’s awesome to have somebody like that as your mentor.”
Coincidentally, De Paula would go on to launch a three-run home run as his first major-league hit, a feat he shares with Heyward — although Heyward did it in his first at-bat.
“It’s a very commendable job that all of our staff have done at every level,” Heyward said. “... I’d be doing a big injustice without giving everyone their flowers on this because it’s definitely been a group effort. … For someone like him who became a part of the organization at 16 years old, he’s a Dodger through and through.”
Over the past week and a half, the major-league coaching staff, which also had De Paula in major-league spring training camp the last two years, has taken over. And already, they’ve seen the benefit of the routine he’s developed this year.
“All the reports that we’ve gotten from our minor-league staff are right on cue,” Ebel said. “He’s been working, he’s bringing it right here to the major leagues. And it’s a pleasure for me, with some energy, coming out early every day — hasn’t missed. We’re working on game situations, ground balls, left, right, right at him, fly balls, shags during BP. So we’re on the right track.”
Dodgers two-time Cy Young winner Blake Snell joined them one day in Miami, catching De Paula’s throws in early work. Though the new teammates wanted to keep the specifics of their conversations between them, Snell’s advice and encouragement made an impression — “It’s like putting fuel in a rocket,” De Paula said.
“He’s just really, really talented, lots to learn,” Snell said. “And excited for him in his journey and what it could turn into.”
In the next city, Cincinnati, Roberts spent an afternoon in left field with him while he was shagging fly balls during batting practice.
“I wanted to be up close to watch him get off on the baseball, watch his reads, his angles to balls and make sure he’s shagging the right way,” Roberts said. “Had some instruction for him; he was great.”
Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers piled up 15 hits in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants with Shohei Ohtani’s return on the horizon.
Roberts, too, has challenged De Paula to make defense a strength, one that will keep him in games, rather than lifted for a defensive replacement. And De Paula has met it with bright eyes and motivation.
“The trust on the defense is going to come,” De Paula said. “I have to prove it over time. And with the work that I’m doing on the field, I know I’m going to gain it.”
A gold glove is a goal of his too.
“That’s one thing about me, when my mind is set on something, I feel like it’s no going back,” De Paula said. “So, I’ve gotten a lot of hate on my defense, and I just love to prove people wrong. So I’m like, hey, all right, there’s a weakness there, but I’m gonna shut you up. Just give me some time. I’ve got you.”

item.content:encoded:
守り抜いたローテーション、山本由伸 明日23日パドレス戦で28度目、レギュラーシーズン最後の先発へ MLB随一の安定感、全体トップQS率は驚異的『77.8』
ドジャースの山本由伸投手が、今季レギュラーシーズン最後の先発登板と予想される明日23日のパドレス戦。今季は開幕から先発ローテーションを守りつづけ、チームトップの28度目の先発マウンドに立つこととなります。
山本投手はドジャースのローテーションを担う先発陣では、唯一ここまで離脱することなくプレーし続けてきました。積み上げた先発登板試合数はチームトップの27試合。しかも好調を維持し続け、投げれば好投を披露。その安定感を証明するかのように、MLB全体トップとなる21度のQSを記録しています。そしてMLB自身キャリアハイの14勝を挙げ、防御率は『2.51』でリーグ3位につけています。
またQS率『77.8』でもMLB全体1位。WHIPは『0.87』でジェーコブ・ミジオロウスキー投手に次ぐリーグ2位(MLB全体でも2位)で、並み居る好投手をしのぐ成績をおさめています。
特に驚異的なのは、シーズン終盤にきても直近の2試合では圧巻の内容。10日のレッズ戦では7回1失点3安打でおさえ、16日のレッズ戦では7回無失点1安打と完璧に相手打線を手玉に取りました。
これまで中6～7日で先発ローテーションを守ってきた山本投手にとっては、明日23日のパドレス戦が今季レギュラーシーズン最後の先発マウンドとなる見込み。どんな投球で締めくくるのか注目されます。

item.content:encoded: レギュラーシーズン終了まで1週間、この選手から目を離すな。MLB公式サイトは現地時間9月20日、全30チームから1人ずつ、最終週で注目すべき選手をピックアップした。日本人選手ではホワイトソックスから村上宗隆、ドジャースから大谷翔平が選ばれた。 【動画】これが見たいんだ！ 大谷翔平の超特大アーチ ホワイトソックスは、ア・リーグ中地区の2位。1ゲーム差の首位ガーディアンズと熾烈な地区優勝争いを繰り広げている。 「ムラカミが打てば、チームも勝つ」 救援右腕マイク・バシルは魔法の杖のパフォーマンスで村上とともにメディアの注目を集めた。その右腕の言葉が村上の重要性を最も的確に表現していると指摘。「ムラカミは日本からの加入によってこのチームを一変させた」と弱小球団を蘇らせた「ムラカミ効果」に言及した。 「ムラカミは8月の初めから不振に苦しんでいたが、9月17日のタイガース戦で復調への兆しとなる特大3ランを放った。最終2カードで調子を取り戻せれば、チームは予想もされなかったプレーオフの切符を手にできるだろう」 3年連続で100敗以上を喫してきたチームだが、地区シリーズで敗退した2021年以来、5年ぶりのプレーオフ進出は、手の届くところにあると強調した。 そして大谷である。こちらは右上腕二頭筋や左膝裏の負傷などで、15日間の負傷者リスト（IL）に入れられている。 「投手としての今季の登板はもうないが、打者としての復帰は予定されている。この最終週は調整のために数試合の出場になるか、ベンチ裏の室内でのスイングの調整になるのか分からないが、彼にとって非常に重要なものになるだろう」 大谷は最短で現地時間23日のパドレス戦でILから復帰が可能になる。実戦の打席に立ってプレーオフへ状態を上げていくのか、それとも投手の映像と実際の投球を再現できるトラジェクトアークでの打席を重ねていくのか、現時点では明確な調整過程は明示されてはいない。それでもどんな形になろうとも、プレーオフで活躍を見せるためにはこの1週間の「中身」が大事になると指摘した。 [文/構成:ココカラネクスト編集部]

item.content:encoded:
By Field Level Media
Sep 22 (Field Level Media) – Pete Alonso’s second home run of the game and 40th of the season lifted the Baltimore Orioles to a 4-3 comeback victory against the visiting Toronto Blue Jays in the opener of a three-game series Monday night.
Alonso’s two-run shot with two outs in the eighth inning gave Baltimore its first lead of the game. The Orioles pulled within 4 1/2 games of the White Sox in the race for the third American League wild card, while the Blue Jays now trail Chicago by 3 1/2 games.
Alonso also homered in the first inning and Gunnar Henderson (3-for-4) went deep in the sixth inning as the Orioles ended a three-game losing streak. Baltimore reliever Yennier Cano (4-3) worked 1 1/3 shutout innings, and Rico Garcia pitched a 1-2-3 ninth for his 10th save.
George Springer had two singles and an RBI for the Blue Jays, who lost for the fifth time in seven games. Tyler Rogers (2-3) gave up the decisive home run.
Tigers 9, Nationals 2
Ben Malgeri hit a three-run home run, Javier Baez and Spencer Torkelson each supplied two-run shots and host Detroit opened a three-game series with a romp over Washington.
River Ryan, elevated from Triple-A, started and pitched three scoreless innings while recording three strikeouts in his Tigers debut. Ryan, acquired in August from the Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal deal, last pitched in the majors in 2024. Keider Montero (10-9) followed with four shutout innings while striking out five.
Pinch hitter Yohandy Morales produced a two-run homer for the Nationals, who took their second loss in a row. DJ Herz (0-1) allowed four runs in four innings during his first major league outing since 2024.
Giants 5, Twins 2
Drew Gilbert homered, collected three hits and drove in a career-high-tying three runs as host San Francisco defeated Minnesota.
Brett Harris chipped in two hits, including a two-run single, as the Giants snapped a three-game losing streak. San Francisco reliever Tristan Beck (1-0) threw 2 2/3 innings of hitless ball, and Trent Harris tossed a perfect ninth inning for his second save.
Brooks Lee and Emmanuel Rodriguez homered for the Twins, who lost for the sixth time in nine games. Zebby Matthews (9-11) fanned nine in five innings but yielded five runs on eight hits.
(–Field Level Media)

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — Shohei Ohtani and the Los Angeles Dodgers will take center stage in the next episode of MLB Clubhouse’s stop-motion series, “The Doug Out!,” scheduled to premiere Tuesday, September 22, at 8:30 a.m. ET on the MLB Clubhouse YouTube channel.
The kid-focused episode presents Ohtani as a baseball superstar whose rare combination of pitching, power hitting and speed makes him one of the sport’s most compelling players. It uses humor, animation and simple explanations to introduce younger viewers to his two-way role.
How the episode introduces Shohei Ohtani
The episode follows host Doug as he tries to match Ohtani’s preparation by taking a series of exaggerated power naps. That running joke leads into a “superstar snapshot” covering Ohtani’s work as a starting pitcher and hitter, along with his home-run power, velocity and speed on the bases.
The story also brings in several parts of Ohtani’s life and Dodgers identity that young fans will recognize. His dog, Decoy, appears in the conversation, while Mookie Betts is highlighted as a teammate and fan favorite.
A separate sketchbook segment explains how a grand slam works by showing the bases loaded and all four runners scoring on one home run. The episode then moves into Dodgers trivia, touching on Dodger Stadium, the franchise’s history and the team’s familiar on-base celebration.
MLB Clubhouse targets baseball’s next generation
“The Doug Out!” is in its inaugural season as a season-long stop-motion series on MLB Clubhouse, a YouTube channel created to help children learn about baseball, its clubs and its biggest personalities.
The Ohtani installment continues MLB’s broader effort to make the sport more accessible to younger audiences through short-form, family-friendly programming. More information about the channel and its programming is available in MLB’s original MLB Clubhouse announcement.
The episode is scheduled to premiere on the MLB Clubhouse YouTube channel Tuesday at 8:30 a.m. ET.

item.title: [whittierdailynews.com] Are the Dodgers finding the best version of themselves just in time?

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The energy emanating from the steamroller heading up I-5 on Monday radiated for miles.
Fuel was used to power the buses the San Diego Padres used to make the trip north for a three-game series that starts Tuesday night, but only because they didn’t try adrenaline.
Winners in 13 of their past 14 games, the Padres are poised to accomplish team history over the next few days. Never in their existence have they made the playoffs in three consecutive seasons.
San Diego has a magic number of two to clinch a National League wild-card spot, although the Padres intend to run through the finish line with a chance at ascending to the top of the wild-card heap in the NL.
“I feel like the whole team is in a good spot right now,” San Diego’s Fernando Tatis Jr. told the San Diego Union-Tribune on Sunday. “We’re playing really good baseball. We’re checking in when we have to. The entire lineup is in a good spot right now. So when it’s going like that, it’s … a good time.”
The Dodgers already have another NL West title secured (their 13th in the past 14 years), but they also have a magic number of three to clinch a top-two seed in the NL playoffs and a bye into one of the best-of-five Division Series.
“I think it’s going to be a good kind of (playoff) primer,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said of the upcoming series. “They’re a very talented team. They’re playing as good as anyone in all of baseball. I’m looking forward to playing those guys and just kind of ramping it up a little bit more for our guys.”
With the Dodgers on a 14-3 run since Sept. 3, they are on a familiar final month charge toward the playoffs. Second-half lulls in each of the past two seasons have transformed into Septembers when the group has discovered the best version of itself.
Last season, the Dodgers were swept in a three-game series by the Angels in August then opened September with a three-game dud in Pittsburgh. A disastrous loss in Baltimore lit the fire after Yoshinobu Yamamoto lost a no-hitter with two outs in the ninth inning and the Dodgers never recorded another out while losing the game.
The wide-awake Dodgers went 15-5 the rest of the way, stormed through the NL playoffs – going 9-1 against the Cincinnati Reds, Philadelphia Phillies and Milwaukee Brewers – then came out on top in a dramatic seven-game World Series against the Toronto Blue Jays.
Earlier this month, it was a brutal 8-6 loss in 10 innings to the St. Louis Cardinals on Sept. 2 that was the wake-up call. It included a four-strikeout night from Shohei Ohtani, who played just one more game before taking his current spot on the injured list.
Properly motivated, the Dodgers have gone on a tear ever since, but it has come at the expense of teams that were not in playoff contention like the Washington Nationals, Reds, Miami Marlins and San Francisco Giants.
This week marks the Dodgers’ first chance to face a team playing at the peak of its powers since they faced the Boston Red Sox, Chicago Cubs, Milwaukee Brewers and Atlanta Braves all in a recent 25-game stretch. They flubbed that test by going 1-12 in those games.
Mookie Betts, Kyle Tucker and Will Smith all have put a charge into the resurgence, while the arrival of rookie Josue De Paula has given the lineup another hitter who can extend at-bats with a discerning eye, along with Max Muncy.
Betts went 0 for 4 in Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, yet he still is hitting .373 with six home runs, 20 RBIs and a 1.215 OPS in 17 games since the start of September.
Far from content with an offense that has averaged 5.8 runs per game this month, Betts said the Dodgers can do even more. After all, Andy Pages is set to return Tuesday, while Ohtani could be back later this week.
“Some guys are hitting, some guys are not,” Betts said. “I think that’s the beauty of the lineup. You get a couple guys going, and a couple guys here can carry a team, and you never know. You just never know who’s it going to be, it’s different guys every day.”
Amid a brutal first season with the Dodgers, Tucker has done his part lately by going 15 for 36 (.417) over his past 11 games with five home runs and 11 RBIs. He was limited to coming off the bench on Sunday after he fouled a ball off his right knee on Saturday.
Tucker was not with the club for last year’s September revival, but he has helped power this one. When it comes to team potential, Tucker is a big-picture guy.
“I think our potential is winning the World Series,” Tucker said. “So (when) we do that, then I can say we reached it. But we feel like we’re in a good spot right now. Our pitching staff’s done a great job all year giving us an opportunity to win every single night. Our defense has played pretty well behind them and then offensively we’ve done a solid job as well.”
“Right now, we got a few guys that are feeling good. A few guys that are banged up. But we’re still out there grinding trying to win as many games as possible before the season ends and just trying to carry it all the way to the playoffs.”
At the very least, confidence will be high this week, in both dugouts.
UP NEXT
Padres (RHP Michael King, 12-9, 3.03 ERA) at Dodgers (TBA), Tuesday, 7:10 p.m., SportsNet LA, 570 AM

item.content:encoded:
DETROIT (AP) — River Ryan was outstanding in his Detroit debut and the Tigers hit three home runs to rout the Washington Nationals 9-2 on Monday night, one day after being eliminated from the American League playoff race.
Ryan, acquired from the Los Angeles Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal trade, pitched three scoreless innings. He allowed two hits and a walk with two strikeouts. Ryan is expected to start again in the season finale Sunday — the day after Justin Verlander is scheduled to make his final major league start.
Keider Montero (10-9) pitched four scoreless innings in relief of Ryan.
Washington starter DJ Herz (0-1) made his first big league appearance in nearly two years. Herz, who had Tommy John surgery in April 2025, pitched four innings, allowing four runs on five hits and two walks while striking out four.
The Tigers took a 2-0 lead in the first. Gleyber Torres walked, went to second on a wild pitch and scored on a ground-rule double from Hao-Yu Lee. After Herz got the first out, Eduardo Valencia singled to left field, with Lee scoring when James Wood misplayed the ball for an error.
Javier Báez made it 4-0 in the fourth, hitting his third homer of the season over the Tigers bullpen in left to bring home Dillon Dingler.
Detroit added five more runs in the fifth, three on Ben Malgeri’s fourth homer and two on Spencer Torkelson’s 25th.
That made it 9-0, but Yohandy Morales hit a two-run homer to get the Nationals on the scoreboard in the eighth.
The Tigers announced before the game that, due to a bank merger, Comerica Park will be known as Fifth Third Park starting in 2027. That’s the same name as the stadium for the Toledo Mud Hens, Detroit’s Triple-A team.
